title: Implement a generic ring buffer in Go
description: Greenfield Go task: implement a generic fixed-capacity ring buffer (circular buffer) with Push, Pop, IsEmpty, and IsFull operations.

task_spec.prompt:
Implement RingBuffer[T any] in ringbuf.go.

type RingBuffer[T any] struct { ... }

func New[T any](capacity int) *RingBuffer[T]
func (rb *RingBuffer[T]) Push(v T) error   // error if full
func (rb *RingBuffer[T]) Pop() (T, error)  // error if empty
func (rb *RingBuffer[T]) IsEmpty() bool
func (rb *RingBuffer[T]) IsFull() bool

Use a fixed-size slice with head/tail indices and a count.
All 5 tests in ringbuf_test.go must pass.
Run: go test ./...
required_artifacts: RingBuffer struct with data slice, head int, tail int, count int
New allocates data slice of given capacity
Push returns error when full, otherwise stores and advances tail mod cap
Pop returns error when empty, otherwise reads head and advances head mod cap
Wrap-around test passes (head/tail cross boundary correctly)
followup_prompts: Run `go test ./...` and show me which tests are passing and which are still failing. Fix any failures — pay attention to edge cases like empty input, boundary values, and error conditions.
Final check: run `go test ./...` one more time. All tests must be green. If anything is still failing, trace through the failing assertion and fix it now.
